paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea, and it's tucked in the middle of a funeral song: God doesn't want Israel's religious trips. He wants Israel. He says, "Seek Me and live!" (Amos 5:4), and then He says it again in different words: "Seek good, not evil, so that you may live." (Amos 5:14). Bethel and Gilgal were places, but life was never in the places. Life is in the LORD.

And here's why that matters to you. The people in this passage kept saying the LORD was with them (Amos 5:14), but they turned justice into wormwood, took bribes, and trampled on the poor (Amos 5:7, 11, 12). Friend, that's wearing the apron and never turning on the oven. Seeking God and loving good go together, so when He says, "Hate evil and love good; establish justice in the gate," (Amos 5:15), He's telling us what seeking Him looks like when we walk out the door.

Now look at that little word again: "Perhaps the LORD, the God of Hosts, will be gracious to the remnant of Joseph." (Amos 5:15). The warning is heavy, and I think it's heavy because He wants them to turn. The same LORD who made the Pleiades and Orion (Amos 5:8) is still calling, and He's still the One to seek. So when your own day gets noisy, baker, go to Him first, and let that shape how you treat the people around you. This story isn't over, because Amos still has more to say.
